concepts.name: Newton's second law F=m*a for constant mass in one dimension

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.
Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.

concepts.name: acceleration as change in velocity over change in time

evidence.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.

objectives: Apply F=m*a with constant mass to find acceleration from net force in one dimension
Define acceleration as (V1-V0)/(t1-t0) and use in second law
Recognize constant-mass requirement for F=m*a form
Recognize force and acceleration as vector quantities applicable per component direction in one dimension
